text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks without cluttering the interface. The trade-off is one extra click for mouse users, but the benefit for screen-reader and keyboard-only users outweighs it.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s hidden until focus—many never tab past the first link. A better alternative is an always-visible skip link styled to blend with the header, so sighted keyboard users see it immediately without sacrificing speed. Settle this by testing with both screen-reader and keyboard-only users to measure bypass success rates.

name: Ramp
text:
Add an always-visible skip link at the top of every page, styled to match the header’s contrast and spacing. This ensures sighted keyboard users see it immediately without extra clicks, while screen-reader users still get the bypass. The trade-off is minimal visual clutter in the header, but the benefit for keyboard navigation and reduced frustration far outweighs it.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users treating the always-visible skip link as decorative—ignoring it because it looks like part of the header. A better alternative is a skip link that appears only on keyboard focus, but with a 100ms delay to ensure screen readers catch it before the user tabs past. Settle this by testing with both keyboard-only and screen-reader users to measure bypass success rates.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a focus-triggered skip link with a 100ms delay—high-contrast, full-width, keyboard-only visible. Result: Skip link appears only on focus (100ms delay) to ensure screen readers catch it before tabbing past. Owner: accessibility-w1.
